findings.reason: The original standalone tiles show the complete interval-overlap formula and proof but no illustration. A common-time-axis schematic materially connects min/max to geometric overlap and distinguishes endpoint contact from positive length. This is a warranted expository addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a defect in the existing formula.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Two closed real time intervals [s,t] and [u,v], with 0<=s<=t and 0<=u<=v; vertical levels distinguish intervals and carry no probabilistic meaning.
diagram_math_checks.check: Each panel projects both intervals onto a shared horizontal time scale. Dots represent included endpoints; neither panel claims equality of Brownian increments.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Upper panel: s=0.7, u=2.6, t=4.5, v=6.4 in drawing coordinates.
diagram_math_checks.check: s<u<t<v. Intersection is [u,t]; the thick axis segment runs exactly from x=2.6 to x=4.5. Thus length=t-u=min(t,v)-max(s,u), matching Verification step 3.1. Dashed guides have matching x coordinates.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Lower panel: s=0.7, t=u=3.5, v=6.4 in drawing coordinates.
diagram_math_checks.check: s<t=u<v. Intersection is the singleton {t}; the axis shows one point, with no thick segment. min(t,v)-max(s,u)=t-u=0, matching step 2.1.

diagram_math_checks.objects: All six strict admissible endpoint orders.
diagram_math_checks.check: s<t<u<v and u<v<s<t give 0; s<u<t<v gives t-u; u<s<v<t gives v-s; s<u<v<t gives v-u; u<s<t<v gives t-s. These equal max(0,min(t,v)-max(s,u)) and follow by four-minimum expansion in step 1.1 and covariance symmetry in step 2.1.

The same inequalities partition after assuming s<=u into t<=u, u<t<=v, and u<=v<t (steps 2.1–4.1). Equal starts or ends do not change the formulas; t=u gives zero; s=t or u=v gives zero; identical intervals give t-s, including all endpoints zero. These cover shared endpoints, containment and degenerate intervals without relying on the picture.

Enumerated all 441 ordered endpoint quadruples on {0,1,2,3,4,5}; the four-minimum expression equals the nonnegative overlap formula in every case. This finite check supplements the symbolic exhaustive case reasoning, rather than proving the real-endpoint result.
